clue.text: Brave tidings given after loyal toast!

definitions.text: Brave tidings given after loyal toast!

parts.words: Brave tidings given after loyal toast!
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior whose tidings travel by puffs from a fire; at a formal dinner, the loyal toast to the monarch is the moment smoking may begin

explanation.surface: News of courage is announced once the guests have drunk to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: At British formal dinners nobody smokes until the loyal toast to the monarch has been drunk, so the 'tidings given after' it are the first lit cigars, while a 'Brave' sends messages by puffs from a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American warrior's message sent by puffs from a fire is the classic image of signalling over distance.

clue.text: The fellow needed for a broadcast?

definitions.text: The fellow needed for a broadcast?

parts.words: The fellow needed for a broadcast?
parts.note: a man's name that is also short for the microphone a broadcaster speaks into

explanation.surface: Which man is essential for putting out a programme?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' points to a man's name; the same word is the short form of microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for microphone, the device every broadcast needs, and also a man's first name.

clue.text: Nut tree left grafted in pieces of oak

indicators.note: grafting sets one shoot into another plant, so one piece goes inside the other
breaking the word into pieces lets its letters be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A tree with a branch grafted into an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' rearranges OAK to KOA, and 'grafted in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African cola tree bears caffeine-rich nuts once used to flavour soft drinks.

clue.text: Check it stands behind the other buildings?

definitions.meaning: a reverse or hindrance

definitions.text: it stands behind the other buildings?
definitions.meaning: a building placed further back from the street than its neighbours

explanation.surface: Inspecting a building that sits behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse that holds progress back is a check; a house built further from the road than its neighbours is set back.

clue.text: Common medal struck for serving meals

definitions.meaning: British slang for a medal or decoration
a metal disc hit to call people to dinner

explanation.surface: An ordinary medal, hit to announce that dinner is served.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a medal is a gong; the brass disc is struck to summon diners.

clue.text: Dreadful, but not for everybody apparently

definitions.meaning: inspiring dread or terror
split into two parts, the word seems to say fear is felt only by some, not all

explanation.surface: Something terrible, though not everyone thinks so.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as AWE + SOME, the word appears to promise awe to some people and not to all, hence 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring awe once meant inspiring dread; split, the word seems to offer awe to some people only, not all.

clue.text: Slowly stretch your legs?

parts.note: to stretch one's legs means to go out walking; doing it slowly is a gentle amble

explanation.surface: Advice to do your leg stretches gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch your legs' sounds like a warm-up exercise, but the idiom means to go for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is the idiom for going out to get some exercise.

clue.text: Chappy lived up to having a colossal nerve!

parts.note: chaps are the jaws or cheeks, so being chappy is being cheeky

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward, in reverse

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow lived up to his reputation for audacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LIVED to give DEVIL; 'chaps' are cheeks, so 'Chappy' gives CHEEKY.
explanation.definitionFit: An impudent rascal is someone with the gall to do or say outrageous things.

clue.text: A form of window decoration

definitions.meaning: a sliding window in a frame raised and lowered by cords
a ribbon worn over the shoulder as an honour or ornament

explanation.surface: A setter describing one style of window dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the sliding frame of a sash window; the other is the ribbon worn across the body with an order of chivalry.

clue.text: It opens a disreputable cupboard-and everything else!

definitions.text: It opens a disreputable cupboard-and everything else!

parts.words: It opens a disreputable cupboard-and everything else!
parts.note: a disreputable cupboard is one with a skeleton in it, a hidden scandal; a key that fits every lock opens everything else too

explanation.surface: Something that unlocks a shameful secret and every other door besides.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'skeleton in the cupboard' is the British idiom for a hidden scandal; a master key filed to fit many locks shares the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass key filed down so that it works many different locks is what burglars and caretakers carry.

clue.text: A holiday in safe territory

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words safe territory

explanation.surface: Taking a break somewhere secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or celebration day, a holiday in the old sense of a feast day.

clue.text: Article guru composed for cultivating good grounds

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled into a new word

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher writes a piece about growing things well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like the guru writing, but it rearranges ARTICLE plus GURU.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming is the tilling of land to produce crops.

clue.text: Upset as Sid going back with musical instrument is first ejected

indicators.note: going back turns the name round so it reads in the reverse direction

parts.note: the organ is a keyboard instrument

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sid is upset at being thrown out of the band as he leaves with his instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses SID to DIS, and 'first' takes the E from 'ejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw into confusion or disorder is to upset an arrangement.

clue.text: The face pulled by a stern pack leader

parts.note: a stern look is a grim one
the ace is the top card of a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: An expression worn by a strict head of a wolf pack or scout troop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack leader' suggests a wolf or a Cub Scout leader, but it is the top card in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted facial expression of pain or disgust is what someone pulls when they make a face.

clue.text: Diplomatic minister's con-eluding verse

definitions.meaning: a diplomat ranking just below an ambassador
the short final stanza of a ballade, also spelt envoi

explanation.surface: The diplomat's closing lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat sent on a mission ranks below an ambassador; the short closing stanza of a poem shares the word.

clue.text: General pardon for little woman brandishing Sten

indicators.note: brandishing is waving something about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Alcott's novel Little Women
taken as written: a Sten is a British sub-machine gun

explanation.surface: A girl waving a gun about earns herself a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brandishing' shuffles AMY (one of the Little Women in Alcott's novel) with STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon granted to a whole class of offenders at once is a general forgiveness by the state.

clue.text: Spring girl bouncing rival

indicators.note: bouncing jumbles the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively girl gets the better of her competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a season here, not a bounce: the girl's name is French for April.
explanation.definitionFit: Avril is a girl's name and the French word for April, a spring month.

clue.text: Rascal heard running through middle of church.

indicators.note: heard signals that the word meant by the following phrase is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the nave is the central body of a church running from the entrance to the chancel

explanation.surface: A rogue is caught dashing up the aisle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the rascal's word is said exactly like the central part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a scoundrel or rogue.

clue.text: A figure tossing coin

indicators.note: tossing throws things into the air, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A shape seen when flipping a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An image or representation, especially a religious picture, is a figure.

clue.text: A railway network that is spread in France

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Describing the French rail system and how far it reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railways until the 1990s; 'spread' is a noun, a soft cheese spread on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese that is spread on bread or crackers.

clue.text: Paper that's not taken seriously

definitions.meaning: a children's paper of strip cartoons
funny, laughable, meant for amusement

explanation.surface: A newspaper nobody treats as serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip-cartoon magazine is a children's paper; the adjective means funny or laughable.

clue.text: Kind of orange put on in East

indicators.note: the answer with the letters of the closing words put on its end becomes the fruit, so they are removed from it

parts.note: a clementine is a small orange
IN as written plus E, the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A variety of orange is put on sale in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: put IN and E (East) on the end of the answer and it becomes CLEMENTINE, a kind of orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or gentle, a kind disposition.

clue.text: Establish a trick business house?

parts.note: a con is a confidence trick
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Setting up a fraudulent company.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something true is to establish or verify it.

clue.text: Only dug-out suitable for heathens

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Only a trench will do for unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug-out' reads as a shelter, but 'out' is the anagram signal over ONLY and DUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irreligious or wicked suits those who do not worship God.

clue.text: Wagnerian rock singers

parts.note: the legend of a siren on a cliff above the Rhine luring boatmen to their death, the river of Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.surface: Singers who perform heavy rock in the style of Wagner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests loud music, but it is a real rock on the Rhine, the river of Wagner's operas, where in legend a maiden sang sailors to their doom.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend the cliff on the Rhine is haunted by a siren whose song wrecks river boatmen.

clue.text: A screw fixer backing big fish

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a nut is threaded onto a screw or bolt to fix it

explanation.surface: A piece of hardware supporting a large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses A plus NUT, giving TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The tunny is a large ocean fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: I object to hush network

parts.note: the objective case of I is me
sh is the sound made to call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at a call for silence across the network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' sounds like a protest, but it is grammar: ME is the object form of I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net or interlaced network of threads.

clue.text: Staunch family main line

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
the main line of descent of a family

explanation.surface: A loyal and true family line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop a flow of blood is to stem it; the main line of a family tree is its stem.

clue.text: Not 30 but not long after

definitions.meaning: not at present, but later
soon, shortly

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: not this moment, but shortly after.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon means soon or presently: not now but in a little while.

clue.text: Monk drunk?

definitions.meaning: a member of the order founded by St Benedict
something drunk: the herbal liqueur first made by the monks of Fecamp

explanation.surface: Is the monk drunk?
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of St Benedict's rule shares the word with the French herb liqueur named after his order.

clue.text: It's uphill going getting a little more money

definitions.meaning: a slope or upward incline
an increase in pay

explanation.surface: Climbing a hill for a modest extra sum.
explanation.definitionFit: An upward slope in a road; and in Britain an increase in wages is a pay rise.

clue.text: Just now, not just then, met a Tom

indicators.note: not just means unfair or wrong, so the letters that follow are put wrongly in order

explanation.surface: Bumping into a man named Tom moments ago, not back then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' looks like part of the definition contrasting now with then, but it is the anagram signal over THEN plus METATOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently, at this time.
